title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #17

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If the skin of a drum is loose, the sound is (1 mark)
   A. lower
   B. higher
   C. the same as a tight skin
   D. louder than a tight skin always

2. To identify an instrument we give its name, its community and (1 mark)
   A. the name of the shop
   B. how it is played
   C. its price
   D. the colour of the shop

3. What does pivoting mean? (1 mark)
   A. Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   B. Dropping the ball
   C. Jumping over the ball
   D. Running quickly

4. How high is the goal ring above the ground? (1 mark)
   A. 3.05 metres
   B. 5 metres
   C. 10 metres
   D. 1.5 metres

5. Where must a player stand to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. Inside the goal circle
   B. At the centre circle
   C. Anywhere on the court
   D. Behind the goal post

6. What can you do to clean your working area after painting? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it messy
   B. Pour paint in a stream where animals drink
   C. Wash brushes and wipe the desk
   D. Throw paint on the floor

7. How many boxes are on the scale strip in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Ten
   B. Five
   C. Two
   D. One

8. When darkening a colour with black, you should add (1 mark)
   A. white first
   B. a little at a time
   C. a whole tin at once
   D. nothing

9. A darker tone of a colour is called a (1 mark)
   A. tint
   B. frame
   C. shade
   D. secondary

10. Where can you get pictures for a montage? (1 mark)
   A. Only from the bank
   B. From the sky
   C. Old newspapers and magazines
   D. From a rock

11. A pair of quavers together lasts (1 mark)
   A. four beats
   B. one beat
   C. half a beat
   D. two beats

12. The French rhythm name for a crotchet is (1 mark)
   A. taa
   B. te-te
   C. ta-te
   D. sh

13. The steady pulse in a piece of music is called the (1 mark)
   A. melody
   B. echo
   C. lyric
   D. beat

14. Which letter has a descender? (1 mark)
   A. g
   B. e
   C. a
   D. k

15. Which is the lowest of the notes d, r and m? (1 mark)
   A. They are all the same
   B. m
   C. r
   D. d

16. The Kodaly hand sign for m is (1 mark)
   A. a flat palm held level
   B. a sloping palm
   C. a closed fist
   D. a wave

17. Which nationality was Zoltan Kodaly, whose method uses hand signs? (1 mark)
   A. Kenyan
   B. Hungarian
   C. Brazilian
   D. Chinese

18. Which move skips over a note? (1 mark)
   A. d to r
   B. r to m
   C. d to m
   D. m to r

19. Why do we knead clay before using it? (1 mark)
   A. To make it black
   B. To make it hard
   C. To make it smooth and remove air
   D. To make it dry

20. The home note of the melodies in this lesson is (1 mark)
   A. none of them
   B. r
   C. m
   D. d

21. On the Kenyan flag, white stands for (1 mark)
   A. blood
   B. peace and honesty
   C. the people
   D. the sky

22. On the Kenyan flag, green stands for (1 mark)
   A. the land and natural wealth
   B. the sun
   C. the rivers only
   D. the people

23. Which is the correct first step in the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Jump high
   B. Lie face down
   C. Sit with knees bent and feet flat
   D. Stand on your head

24. In a partner check for the crab balance, how many touching points does the table have? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Six
   C. Four
   D. Eight

25. A song about washing hands to prevent germs is a (1 mark)
   A. funeral song
   B. topical song
   C. naming song
   D. marriage song

26. Unison singing is suitable for an anthem because (1 mark)
   A. it needs instruments
   B. everyone can join in the same tune
   C. it uses no notes
   D. it is silent

27. Gestures in singing are (1 mark)
   A. quiet time
   B. hand and body movements that fit the song
   C. words only
   D. sounds of the drum

28. The mood of a song is (1 mark)
   A. its length in metres
   B. the name of the composer
   C. its price
   D. the feeling it gives

29. Which is a patriotic song? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya National Anthem
   B. A hymn of worship only
   C. A lullaby about sleeping
   D. A drum solo

30. Indoors, the best place to stand for better light is (1 mark)
   A. in a dark corner
   B. in the cupboard
   C. near a window or open door
   D. under a table

31. The bottom part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. head joint
   B. thumb hole
   C. foot joint
   D. beak

32. Of the notes B, A and G, which is the highest? (1 mark)
   A. G
   B. A
   C. They are equal
   D. B

33. The top part of the recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. middle joint
   B. head joint
   C. bell
   D. foot joint

34. Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1 and 2 covered? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. G
   C. D
   D. B

35. What sound do you hear if a hole is not fully covered? (1 mark)
   A. A clear note
   B. Nothing at all
   C. A drum sound
   D. A squeak or weak sound

36. Prone means (1 mark)
   A. sitting
   B. face up
   C. standing
   D. face down

37. Why are indigenous games part of our heritage? (1 mark)
   A. They were bought yesterday
   B. They come to us from earlier generations
   C. They have no meaning
   D. They are foreign

38. Which game builds strong arms and shoulders as you crawl on hands and toes? (1 mark)
   A. Giraffe stretch
   B. Elephant walk
   C. Snake slither
   D. Crocodile crawl

39. Learning about animals in games links to (1 mark)
   A. Agriculture
   B. Weather forecasts
   C. Swimming lessons only
   D. Space travel

40. A portfolio is (1 mark)
   A. a folder for keeping creative works together
   B. a ball
   C. a kind of paint
   D. a song

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. State four rules of netball. (4 marks)

42. Give three qualities of a neat montage. (3 marks)

43. State three qualities of good feedback. (3 marks)

44. State three occasions when the Kenya National Anthem is sung. (3 marks)

45. Explain how to take a portrait of a friend with good light and a clear centre of interest. (5 marks)

46. Explain how working in pairs helps when learning the crab balance. (3 marks)

47. Describe the Kodaly hand sign for each of d, r and m. (3 marks)

48. Describe how to do the crab walk and name the muscles it strengthens. (3 marks)

49. Describe the steps of modelling the letters d, r and m on clay slabs. (5 marks)

50. State three points of good sprinting technique. (3 marks)

51. What are ascenders and descenders in lettering? Give one example of each. (3 marks)

52. Describe three qualities of a good rhythmic pattern. (3 marks)

53. Why should a composed rhythm be your own idea? (2 marks)

54. State four performance techniques for a good singer. (4 marks)

55. Name two types of songs learnt in this topic other than folk songs. (2 marks)

56. Give four safety rules for animal games. (4 marks)

57. Describe how to make a ball using the macramé technique and overhand knots. (5 marks)

58. How should clay models be dried and why? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — lower
   A loose skin vibrates more slowly, so the sound is lower.

2. B — how it is played
   Identifying uses name, community and method of playing.

3. A — Turning on the landing foot without moving it
   A player keeps one foot down and turns on it.

4. A — 3.05 metres
   The netball goal ring is 3.05 metres high.

5. A — Inside the goal circle
   Shots must be taken from inside the goal circle.

6. C — Wash brushes and wipe the desk
   Clean-up shows responsibility.

7. B — Five
   The strip is divided into five equal boxes.

8. B — a little at a time
   Black is strong, so add it in small amounts.

9. C — shade
   Adding black makes a shade.

10. C — Old newspapers and magazines
   Cut pictures from old papers and magazines.

11. B — one beat
   Two half beats make one whole beat.

12. A — taa
   Taa is the name for one long sound in one beat.

13. D — beat
   The beat is the steady pulse we tap or clap along to.

14. A — g
   The tail of g goes below the baseline.

15. D — d
   Doh is the lowest of the three.

16. A — a flat palm held level
   Me is shown with a flat, level hand.

17. B — Hungarian
   Zoltan Kodaly was a Hungarian music teacher.

18. C — d to m
   Going from d to m skips r.

19. C — To make it smooth and remove air
   Kneading makes clay smooth and easy to shape.

20. D — d
   Melodies feel finished when they end on d.

21. B — peace and honesty
   White stands for peace and honesty.

22. A — the land and natural wealth
   Green stands for the land and its natural wealth.

23. C — Sit with knees bent and feet flat
   You start sitting with knees bent and feet flat.

24. C — Four
   The table has four legs, two hands and two feet.

25. B — topical song
   It gives a message about a topic of importance.

26. B — everyone can join in the same tune
   A single tune that everybody sings is simple and strong.

27. B — hand and body movements that fit the song
   Gestures help tell the story of a song.

28. D — the feeling it gives
   Mood is the feeling of a song, such as joy or calm.

29. A — Kenya National Anthem
   The anthem is a patriotic song.

30. C — near a window or open door
   Daylight helps.

31. C — foot joint
   The foot joint ends in the bell.

32. D — B
   Fewer covered holes give a higher note.

33. B — head joint
   The head joint has the mouthpiece.

34. A — A
   A uses thumb, 1 and 2.

35. D — A squeak or weak sound
   Leaks make squeaks.

36. D — face down
   Prone is face down.

37. B — They come to us from earlier generations
   Heritage is what we inherit.

38. D — Crocodile crawl
   Body held straight on hands and toes.

39. A — Agriculture
   Agriculture teaches about animals.

40. A — a folder for keeping creative works together
   It protects and presents works.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: No running with the ball; pass or shoot within three seconds; no contact; defenders stand 0.9 metres away; start with a centre pass. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clean cut edges, no glue marks, well-overlapped pieces, firmly stuck and a clear title. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kind, honest, specific and helpful. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: School assembly, Madaraka Day, Mashujaa Day, Jamhuri Day, sports events and other official ceremonies. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission. Put the sun behind you so light falls on the friend's face. Choose a plain background. Move closer so the face fills the picture. Hold the device steadily, press gently and check the photograph.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: One learner performs while the other watches and checks, gives feedback, and helps if needed. They swap places.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: d is a closed fist, r is a sloping palm, m is a flat palm held level.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit, put hands behind, lift the hips and walk on hands and feet with tummy up. It strengthens the arms, shoulders and tummy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the position, 1 mark for walking, 1 mark for muscles.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare and knead clay. Roll a slab and cut three rectangles of different sizes. Make coils. Shape a coil into each letter and scratch and wet where they join. Press on gently, smooth, and let dry slowly in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for preparing clay, cutting slabs, making coils, joining, and drying.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eyes look ahead; elbows bent and arms swing back and forth; knees lift high; land on the front of the foot; body leans forward slightly. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: An ascender is the part of a letter that goes up above the small letters, such as b. A descender goes below the baseline, such as p.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for correct examples.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has variation of note values, repetition of a group of notes and ends on a long note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: Copying is not fair and honest. Your own idea shows integrity and creativity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Good posture; deep breathing; clear diction; gestures; facial expression; eye contact. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sacred songs, patriotic songs and topical songs. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Play on soft, clear ground; warm up; keep a distance from others; do not push or trip; drink water; follow the whistle. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a firm core from paper or cloth. Cut equal cords. Tie them together with an overhand knot at the middle. Put the core on top. Tie overhand knots between pairs of neighbouring cords to make a net around the core. Gather the cords at the bottom and tie a strong knot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five clear stages.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: Slowly in the shade. Strong sun dries them too fast and makes them crack.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
